cells.tense: The exchange between you and the people around you is running even, right now, and you can feel it.
cells.ask: Take one fair arrangement you and someone else already settled — how the load splits, who pays for what — and set it somewhere you both can reach. Then leave it a week with no one watching it.
cells.core:
Whatever couldn't hold has fallen away, and what's standing in the clearing is even. You give, you get, and the people beside you aren't being spent as fuel or spending you. That isn't common, and it isn't luck exactly — a balance is being held by hands, and one of the hands is yours.

The subtle risk now is drift. Arrangements like this tend to hold while somebody is watching and quietly rot when the watcher turns away. So take one thing the two of you settled evenly — not the whole picture, a single item — and put it somewhere both of you can find it, with nothing added about who tends it. Then stop tending it for a week. If it stays even unwatched, the form is holding. If it tips, you'll see where it lives before it costs you anything.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange is even — now see if it holds that way unwatched.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving, kept even between people
cells.place: Where something false has just fallen away

cells.tense: You are already braced for how the next stretch of giving and taking will go wrong.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Meet your own obligations fully for one week, keeping no running count of anyone else's. On the last day, look once at whatever went uncovered and settle it then.
cells.core:
The clearing is real, and what came after it should be an easy give-and-take. Instead you're out ahead of it, tracking who gave what, who still owes, who didn't show up — the audit runs while the exchange is happening. That's fairness doing its job past the point where it helps. The scale is audible to the people on the other side, and the easy flowing back and forth keeps stopping for a count.

There's another way to hold the same ground: your part, fully carried, no running total of the rest. Put the scoreboard down for a week and just meet your obligations. Not a test of them — a week of not reckoning. At the end you'll know, without having watched, where the exchange actually tipped, and you can sort that out once. The evenness you're protecting doesn't need guarding mile by mile.

cells.tense: The clearing happened, but your part in the exchange is still standing at a door that closed behind it.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Look hard at whatever you do for others that brings nothing back, until you can name what it actually gives you — then set it down.
cells.core:
Something false fell away, and the people near you are trading fairly in the open space it left. You're not quite in that. You hand something over and it doesn't complete — generosity arrives from others and doesn't land, or you don't let it. Not coldness; you're capable here. It's that exchange runs mostly one way on your side, and its other direction has gone quiet.

So sort carefully before asking for anything more. Choose the effort you're putting out that gives nothing back and study it until the distinction is sharp — that's the whole act; then set it down. Refined by that much, the picture gets smaller and clearer: which effort was moving something, and which was only covering. Attention like that is what this needs, because what's starved here isn't effort or feeling. It's the judgment about what's actually exchanging.

cells.tense: The fairness in this clearing is kept by a hand you don't quite count as yours.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Before the next honest word you're about to say, wait a breath — just long enough to notice yourself weighing it — then say what you meant, or don't.
cells.core:
Where the false structure fell, the exchange is being balanced, and the balancing is yours — stepping up where something's short, holding back so somebody else gets theirs. What you'd call it is that things just work out, or that these people are easy to be around. They may well be. Still, the evenness has a keeper, and the keeper answers to your name.

There's a habit in that. Before you say what you think is fair, the judgment waits — weighed, checked, sometimes shelved — and you'd tell it you've learned to pick your moments. Maybe. Also maybe the weighing was once a shield, and now it runs on after the reason has cleared. So the practice is small: before the next honest word, one breath of noticing. Not revealing more than you meant. Just standing beside the call you keep making.
